definition: The Rabbit r1 is an artificial intelligence personal assistant device developed by the American technology startup Rabbit Inc and co-designed by Teenage Engineering.
details: It was announced at the 2024 Consumer Electronics Show as a handheld device intended to perform digital tasks through voice commands, touch interaction, and web-based AI agents. The r1 was marketed around Rabbit's concept of a "large action model" (LAM), which the company described as software able to operate websites and services on behalf of users. The device runs rabbitOS, an operating system based on the Android Open Source Project. Its services have included AI search, image recognition, voice interaction, music playback, rideshare and food-ordering integrations, and later experimental web-agent features such as LAM Playground and teach mode. Rabbit continued to issue software updates after launch, including rabbitOS 2 in September 2025, which introduced a redesigned card-based interface, gesture navigation, and a "creations" feature for generating small software tools and experiences on the device. Rabbit Inc was founded by Jesse Lyu Cheng.

explainer.lead: The Rabbit r1 is a handheld AI assistant device marketed around a “large action model” that operates websites and services for the user. It was announced at CES 2024 and runs rabbitOS on the Android Open Source Project.

tiers.eli5: It’s like a small pocket gadget you talk to, and it tries to do things on websites for you.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers integrate voice commands, touch interaction, and web-based AI agents into a single device; a pitfall is that the large-action-model concept depends on reliably operating third-party websites and services.
tiers.paperLevel: An artificial intelligence personal assistant device developed by Rabbit Inc and co-designed by Teenage Engineering, running rabbitOS based on the Android Open Source Project, with services including AI search, image recognition, and voice interaction, marketed around a “large action model” described as software able to operate websites and services on behalf of users.

explainer.example: A user speaks a request into the r1, and the device’s AI agent attempts to carry out the task on a website through voice and touch interaction.
